incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 INCIDENT — elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects observed across gateway cluster (prod). Alerting on-call. root_ts=4112345678
sarah (oncall): seeing lots of client-cancelled + 502s on streaming routes. Dashboard: streaming success rate dropped from 99.6% -> 94.1 around 10:12 UTC.
sanjay (eng-runtime): any recent deploys to gateway or stream handler?
maria (infra): pushed a config tweak to ingress-nginx 10:05 UTC (keepalive pool size change) — I can roll it back quickly if we think it's related.
sarah (oncall): correlating traces now — chunked-encoding partial frames and then client disconnects. Common pattern: gateway returns 502/504 OR connection closes mid-chunk.
sanjay (eng-runtime): can you paste a representative log?
sarah (oncall): sure, tail from gateway logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:21Z ERROR stream_muxer: upstream reset by peer, client_ip=1.2.3.4 route=/v1/stream generate, upstream=stream-handler-3
2026-03-15T10:12:21Z WARN http: client disconnected while streaming, req_id=abc123, reason=client_cancelled
2026-03-15T10:12:22Z ERROR gateway: 502 Bad Gateway from upstream stream-handler-3, latency=12ms
```
sanjay (eng-runtime): looks like upstream stream-handler instances are dropping connections or hitting an internal timeout. Any OOMs or restarts?
maria (infra): no OOMs but I see a spike in open connections and TCP FIN resets on the gateway nodes at 10:12 UTC. Kernel-level counters: tcp_retrans_out increased.
dave (eng-sre): could be a connection storm causing upstreams to saturate ephemeral ports or file descriptors. What's the current per-pod ulimit and keepalive setting?
sanjay (eng-runtime): stream-handler pods have default ulimit, not tuned. Also we rolled in an optimization that flushes chunks more aggressively two days ago — might be exposing client networking issues.
sarah (oncall): customer impact: realtime streaming sessions failing intermittently. Affected ~4% of active streaming sessions; a few customers reported retries, one reported degraded UX (long pauses). Top affected tenants: ["AcmeCorp", "BetaWriter"].
incident-bot: pager triggered: page dave (eng-sre) and sanjay (eng-runtime).
dave (eng-sre): I'm on it. Quick mitigation proposal: 1) revert ingress-nginx keepalive tweak 2) throttle incoming streaming concurrency at gateway 3) increase upstream idle timeout to avoid mid-chunk resets.
maria (infra): I can rollback keepalive in 60s. Rolling back will be a configmap update: `kubectl apply -f ingress-keepalive-rollback.yaml` and then `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/ingress-nginx -n ingress`.
sanjay (eng-runtime): Also let's temporarily enable streaming fallback: if chunked stream fails, gateway should switch to paged response for new requests. I'll flip the feature flag for 5 minutes. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/gateway FEATURE_STREAM_FALLBACK=true -n production && kubectl rollout restart deployment/gateway -n production`
sarah (oncall): doing traffic annotation: adding route weight to fallback for < 5% of traffic while we monitor.
(2 minutes later)
maria (infra): ingress keepalive rollback applied, restarted ingress-nginx. Watching connection counters.
dave (eng-sre): throttling incoming streaming concurrency: set nginx limit_conn to 500 per worker. Applied via configmap.
sanjay (eng-runtime): feature flag toggled to enable fallback. Gateway restarted.
sarah (oncall): monitoring metrics: error rate dropping from 5.9% -> 2.2% within 3 minutes. Partial improvement.
sanjay (eng-runtime): I'm also pushing a hotfix to stream-handler to make chunk flushes tolerant to premature client closes — small change to ignore EPIPE during last-chunk flush. Patch: `git checkout -b fix/stream-epipe && apply patch && kubectl rollout restart deployment/stream-handler -n production`
dave (eng-sre): rolling a controlled restart of stream-handler can help; let's do it one pod at a time. I'll coordinate.
(15 minutes later)
sarah (oncall): follow-up metrics: streaming success rate back to 99.2%. TCP retransmits reduced. No new customer complaints in last 10m.
maria (infra): kernel-level FIN resets normalized. No node reboots required.
sanjay (eng-runtime): hotfix deployed to 3/3 stream-handler pods, observed fewer upstream resets in logs.
sarah (oncall): customer impact summary for post-incident notes: ~4% active streaming sessions experienced partial disconnects between 10:12-10:30 UTC, peak error rate ~6%. No data loss reported; most clients retried successfully or fell back to paged route. Affected customers: AcmeCorp (brief degraded UX, automatic retry recovered), BetaWriter (saw repeated chunk cancels, support notified).
dave (eng-sre): next actions for handoff: 1) Increase stream-handler FD/uplink ulimits and add a preflight test for keepalive changes; 2) Add a circuit-breaker on gateway for aggressive client cancels to avoid upstream saturation; 3) Postmortem with timeline and runbook updates for streaming incidents.
sarah (oncall): handing off to dave (eng-sre) for overnight monitoring and follow-up. Key artifacts attached: dashboard link https://app.redwood.example/d/streams/stream-health, logs query, rollout IDs.
dave (eng-sre): got it — I'll own the postmortem and follow-up with infra/engineers tomorrow. If anything degrades, re-page. Leaving notes:
```
Handoff -> dave (eng-sre) 2026-03-15T10:45Z
Actions taken:
- Rollback ingress keepalive config
- Throttled streaming concurrency at ingress
- Enabled gateway fallback to paged responses temporarily
- Deployed stream-handler hotfix to tolerate EPIPE on chunk flush
Metrics -> success rate recovered to 99.2% within 15m
Customer impact -> low (no data loss), 2 customers with degraded UX flagged
```
sarah (oncall): tagging this as resolved for live mitigation. Will open incident ticket for full postmortem. :white_check_mark:
dave (eng-sre): adding follow-up tasks in Jira and assigning to @sanjay and @maria.
incident-bot: incident P1 marked: mitigated -> handoff complete.
